subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw expose a request-scoped global agent dry-run/no-side-effects mode, and which tool surfaces and hook behaviors must it cover before adding `openclaw agent --dry-run`?
rationale: The request would become a user-trusted security boundary, and current source shows multiple execution surfaces that an adapter-only or process-global flag would not safely cover.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, deferred-tool, and hook behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader workflow modes
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until the broader Ask/Plan/Modify or scoped-agent-mode direction defines shared preview semantics.

options.title: Keep only scoped dry-runs
options.body: Reject a global mode if maintainers decide it is too easy to confuse with sandboxing, and continue improving command-specific preview paths instead.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with tests for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, deferred-tool, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/security-contract choice spanning the CLI, agent runtime, and Gateway surfaces where this handle has strong history.
